heroLead: White Earth is a small community in northern Mountrail County, and the families who hold mineral rights out here often don't realize how solidly they sit inside the Bakken's core.
intro: It doesn't take the same name recognition as Parshall or Stanley to sit on productive ground, and northern Mountrail County has seen real horizontal development over the years. If your family inherited a fraction of an interest near White Earth and never had it properly checked, there's a real chance it's worth more attention than it's gotten.

sections.heading: Northern Mountrail County's overlooked acreage
paragraphs: Development here has generally followed the same pattern as the rest of the county, dense horizontal drilling since the mid-2000s, though White Earth doesn't carry the same name recognition as the fields further south. We check your tract's actual well history rather than assume based on how well-known the area is.

sections.heading: What we need to research your interest
paragraphs: A legal description from an old deed, lease, or Division Order is the fastest way for us to confirm what wells are tied to your interest through the Mountrail County Recorder and the state's well index, before we say what we think it's worth.

sections.heading: Generational ownership around White Earth
paragraphs: Like most of Mountrail County, White Earth-area mineral rights tend to trace back to an original homestead patent, with ownership divided among children and grandchildren over the decades. It's common for owners to hold a modest fraction split several ways, sometimes without every family member aware of the others.
We can research the full ownership picture and work with all co-owners together if your family would rather handle the sale as a group.
